title: Payer Relations Memo: A New Primary Coverage During a Home Oxygen Therapy Rental
content:
# A New Primary Coverage During a Home Oxygen Therapy Rental

## Clauses

1. When a different primary coverage starts paying for Home Oxygen Therapy:
   > Clause retired in part: "a new payment period begins under it on the first date of service it covers." This clause is no longer in force for a change of primary coverage that the patient confirms for the oxygen, on which the oxygen record is moved to the new coverage. Every other change of primary coverage remains under this clause.
2. Months paid under the earlier coverage do not count toward the new cap.
3. The new coverage pays only when the class's coverage-entry requirement is met by a qualifying test within the lookback before the change.
4. The oxygen moves to the new coverage only once that coverage is verified: the new coverage record is in status active. The basis is the system record: the status of the new coverage record.

## Points of judgement

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Do months paid under the earlier coverage count toward the cap under the new coverage? | no |
| What must the new coverage see before it pays? | a qualifying test within the lookback before the change |
| What must the new coverage record show before the oxygen moves to it? | status active |

## Hypothetical illustration

A patient with 20 paid months under an earlier coverage changes primary coverage. Under the new coverage the paid-month count toward the new cap does not include those 20 months. If the new coverage record is not yet in status active, the oxygen does not move to it.
